items.statement: Ensure the safety and quality of every drug the site makes.
items.quote: Drug manufacturers are required to ensure the safety and quality of their drugs.

items.statement: Ensure products, whether marketed under approved applications or not (including over-the-counter monograph products), conform to appropriate quality specifications.
items.quote: FDA reminds manufacturers of drugs marketed under approved applications and manufacturers of other drugs, including over-the-counter monograph drug products, of their obligation to ensure their products conform to appropriate quality specifications.

items.statement: Where benzene can form from benzoate and rise over shelf life, take this into account when deciding when to test for benzene (for example at release and on stability) and when setting an appropriate expiration date.
items.quote: The formation of benzene from benzoate can lead to an increase in benzene content over a drug’s shelf-life and should be considered when determining the appropriate timing for benzene testing, e.g., testing at release and on stability (21 CFR 211.165, 211.166), and establishment of an appropriate expiration date (21 CFR 211.137).
items.condition: where benzene can form from benzoate

items.statement: Give extra scrutiny to the potential risk of benzene contamination whenever raw materials change during the product lifecycle, including a change of raw material supplier.
items.quote: FDA reminds manufacturers that changes in raw materials throughout the lifecycle of the drug, including changes in raw material suppliers, warrant additional scrutiny for the potential risk of benzene contamination.
items.condition: when raw materials or their suppliers change

items.statement: For drug products at risk of benzene contamination, test the products for benzene accordingly.
items.quote: Manufacturers of drug products at risk for benzene contamination should test their drugs accordingly
items.condition: products at risk of benzene contamination

items.statement: For drug products at risk of benzene contamination, do not release any batch that would expose consumers to more than 20 mcg of benzene per day from the product.
items.quote: should not release any drug product batch that would expose consumers to more than 20 mcg per day of benzene from the product
items.condition: products at risk of benzene contamination

items.statement: For at-risk products with a 10 g daily dose, limit benzene to no more than 2 ppm.
items.quote: For products that have a 10 g daily dose, this means that benzene levels should be limited to no more than 2 ppm.
items.condition: products with a 10 g daily dose

items.statement: For at-risk products with a daily dose above 10 g, set a product-specific benzene concentration limit that ensures consumers are not exposed to more than 20 mcg of benzene per day from the product.
items.quote: For products that have a daily dose above 10 g, manufacturers should determine the appropriate concentration limit for their product that ensures consumers are not exposed to more than 20 mcg per day of benzene from the product.

items.statement: If any batches already in distribution contain benzene above the acceptable level, contact the appropriate FDA field quality operations division to discuss voluntarily starting a recall.
items.quote: If any drug product batches containing benzene above this level are already in distribution, the manufacturer should contact the appropriate Division of Pharmaceutical Quality Operations in the Office of Inspections and Investigations (OII) at FDA to discuss the voluntary initiation of a recall.
items.condition: distributed batches exceed the benzene level

items.statement: If a decision not to release a product or to start a recall is likely to disrupt the drug supply, contact FDA's drug shortages staff immediately by email.
items.quote: If decisions to not release a drug product or to initiate a recall are likely to disrupt the drug supply, manufacturers should contact CDER’s Drug Shortages Staff immediately at drugshortages@fda.hhs.gov.
items.condition: non-release or recall likely to disrupt supply

items.statement: Holders of new or abbreviated drug applications must submit a Field Alert Report if testing shows that one or more distributed batches fail their application specification; for products at risk of benzene contamination this covers benzene above 2 ppm or, for products with daily doses of more than 10 g, benzene above the level that would expose consumers to more than 20 mcg per day.
items.quote: NDA and ANDA holders are required to submit a Field Alert Report (FAR) if testing reveals that one or more distributed batches of a drug product fails to meet the specification established for it in the application (21 CFR 314.81(b)(1)(ii)). For products at risk of benzene contamination, this would encompass products for which testing reveals benzene above 2 ppm, or, for drug products that have daily doses of more than 10 g, if testing reveals benzene above the level that would expose consumers to more than 20 mcg per day from the product.
items.condition: distributed batches fail the application specification

items.statement: Manufacturers of products not marketed under an application, including over-the-counter monograph products, should contact FDA through the designated contact route when testing reveals benzene in a product.
items.quote: Manufacturers of nonapplication products, including over-the-counter monograph drug products, should contact FDA using the information in the table below when testing reveals benzene in a product.
items.condition: testing reveals benzene in a nonapplication product

items.statement: Be prepared to give FDA the test results and any available information on the potential source of the benzene.
items.quote: Manufacturers should also be prepared to provide FDA with test results and any information available on the potential source of the benzene to assist in FDA’s analysis.

items.statement: Where batches already in distribution contain benzene above 2 ppm (or, for products with a daily dose of more than 10 g, above the level that would expose consumers to more than 20 mcg per day), contact the appropriate FDA field division recall coordinators.
items.quote: Contact appropriate OII Division Recall Coordinators
items.condition: distributed batches above the benzene level

items.statement: Holders of new or abbreviated drug applications must submit Field Alert Reports for distributed products with benzene findings above the acceptable level.
items.quote: Field Alert Reports are required for ANDAs and NDAs with such findings for distributed drug products (21 CFR 314.81(b)(1)).
items.condition: distributed products with such benzene findings

items.statement: Application holders notified by the manufacturer of an API used in their product of benzene results must submit Field Alert Reports.
items.quote: Application holders notified of benzene results from the manufacturer of an API used in their product are required to submit FARs.
items.condition: notified of benzene results by the API manufacturer
